plain: Soft words turn the heat down. When someone comes at you hot, a gentle answer cools the room. A harsh word pours gas on the fire. You get to choose which one you hand them. ... A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger. Proverbs 15, verse 1. ... Think on this. Who do you need to answer softly this week?

Let your words build, not break. Before it leaves your mouth, ask one question: will this build them up, or tear them down? Words should hand people grace, not wounds. ... Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth, but that which is good to the use of edifying, that it may minister grace unto the hearers. Ephesians 4, verse 29. ... Think on this. Before you speak today, will you ask yourself if it builds?

Your words are seeds. Every word you speak plants something, life or death, in the people around you and in yourself. And you will eat what you plant. ... Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof. Proverbs 18, verse 21. ... Think on this. What have your words been planting at home lately?

Kind words are medicine. A pleasant word is sweet like honey. It can calm a heart, lift a tired body and heal what a hard day broke. ... Pleasant words are as an honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones. Proverbs 16, verse 24. ... Think on this. Who needs a sweet word from you today?

Listen first. Talk second. Most arguments go wrong because both people are waiting to talk. Slow down. Hear the whole thing. Anger cools when people feel heard. ... Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath: James 1, verse 19. ... Think on this. Who do you need to really listen to before you answer?

Season it with grace. Salt makes food better, and grace makes words land. You can say the hard thing and still say it with grace. ... Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man. Colossians 4, verse 6. ... Think on this. What hard thing can you say with more grace?

One mouth, two kinds of water? We praise God on Sunday and cut people down on Monday. The same mouth that blesses should not curse. God can change both. ... Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be. James 3, verse 10. ... Think on this. Where does your mouth need to match your praise?

Be kind at home too. It is easy to be sweet to strangers and sharp with family. Tenderhearted starts with the people who see you every day. ... And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you. Ephesians 4, verse 32. ... Think on this. Who at home needs your kindest words this week?

Some words cut like a sword. Careless words can stab, even when you were only joking. Wise words do the opposite. They heal. ... There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health. Proverbs 12, verse 18. ... Think on this. Is there a word you said that you need to make right?

Ask God to guard your mouth. You don't have to do this alone. Ask the Lord to stand at the door of your lips and stop what shouldn't come out. ... Set a watch, O Lord, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips. Psalm 141, verse 3. ... Think on this. Will you pray this verse before your next hard conversation?

Truth, spoken in love. Kind does not mean fake. God wants the truth told, but carried in love, so it helps the person grow instead of crushing them. ... But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things, which is the head, even Christ: Ephesians 4, verse 15. ... Think on this. What truth do you need to speak, in love?

Don't trade insult for insult. When someone throws an ugly word, you don't have to throw one back. Bless them instead. That is how you inherit a blessing. ... Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that ye are thereunto called, that ye should inherit a blessing. 1 Peter 3, verse 9. ... Think on this. Who can you bless instead of answer back?

The right word at the right time. A word said at the right moment is like gold set in silver. Sometimes the kindest thing is waiting for the right time to say it. ... A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver. Proverbs 25, verse 11. ... Think on this. Who needs a well-timed word of hope from you?

The law of kindness on your tongue. The woman of Proverbs 31 opened her mouth with wisdom, and kindness was the rule she spoke by. Let kindness be your rule too. ... She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness. Proverbs 31, verse 26. ... Think on this. What would change if kindness were the rule for everything you say?

What charity really is. In the King James Bible, charity means love that gives itself away. It is God's own kind of love put into action. It is bigger than a donation. It is a heart that moves toward people. ... And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity. 1 Corinthians 13, verse 13. ... Think on this. Where is God asking your love to move toward someone?

Giving without love is empty. You can give everything away and still miss it. God looks at the heart behind the gift. Without love, it profits nothing. ... And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing. 1 Corinthians 13, verse 3. ... Think on this. Is love behind what you give, or something else?

How to recognize charity. Charity is patient. It is kind. It isn't jealous or showy. It doesn't push its own way, doesn't snap, and doesn't keep thinking the worst. That is how you know it is real. ... Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil; 1 Corinthians 13, verse 4 through 5. ... Think on this. Which of these does God want to grow in you?

Give in secret. Real charity doesn't need a camera. Give quietly, so even your left hand doesn't know. Your Father sees in secret, and He rewards openly. ... But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth: That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly. Matthew 6, verse 3 through 4. ... Think on this. What can you give this week that nobody will ever know about?

God loves a cheerful giver. Don't give because you feel forced or guilty. Decide in your heart, then give with joy. God loves it when we give gladly. ... Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver. 2 Corinthians 9, verse 7. ... Think on this. What would it look like to give with joy this week?

When you give to the poor, you lend to God. Helping someone in need is never wasted. God takes it as a loan to Him, and He always pays back. ... He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord; and that which he hath given will he pay him again. Proverbs 19, verse 17. ... Think on this. Who in need can you show pity to this week?

Charity has hands and feet. Love isn't only something we say. It shows up. It brings the meal, makes the call, pays the bill, sits with the sick. ... My little children, let us not love in word, neither in tongue; but in deed and in truth. 1 John 3, verse 18. ... Think on this. What is one deed of love you can do today?

Don't just say, be blessed. If someone is hungry and cold, telling them to be warm and full doesn't help. Charity meets the actual need in front of you. ... If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit? James 2, verse 15 through 16. ... Think on this. What real need around you can you meet?

You did it unto Him. Jesus said every meal, every visit, every coat given to the least person counts as done for Him. Charity is how we serve Jesus face to face. ... And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. Matthew 25, verse 40. ... Think on this. Who is the least of these that God has put near you?

The widow's two coins. A poor widow gave two small coins, all she had. Jesus said she gave more than all the rich. God measures what it cost you, not the size of the gift. ... And he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: Mark 12, verse 43. ... Think on this. What small gift could you give that would really cost you something?

Go, and do the same. A man was beaten and left on the road. The religious people passed by. A stranger stopped, cleaned his wounds and paid for his care. Jesus said, be like him. ... And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise. Luke 10, verse 37. ... Think on this. Who have you been walking past that you need to stop for?

Don't hold back good. If you can help and it is in your hand to do it, don't wait. Charity doesn't put off what it can do today. ... Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of thine hand to do it. Proverbs 3, verse 27. ... Think on this. What good is in your hand to do right now?

Love covers. Fervent charity doesn't go around exposing people's faults. It covers, forgives and keeps loving. That is how families and churches hold together. ... And above all things have fervent charity among yourselves: for charity shall cover the multitude of sins. 1 Peter 4, verse 8. ... Think on this. Whose faults can you cover with love instead of exposing?

More blessed to give. Jesus said giving brings a deeper blessing than receiving. Support the weak, and you will find joy you can't buy. ... I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive. Acts 20, verse 35. ... Think on this. When did giving bless you more than getting?

What charity looks like. Isaiah paints it plain: bread for the hungry, a home for the one put out, a coat for the cold, and never hiding from your own family when they need you. ... Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh? Isaiah 58, verse 7. ... Think on this. Which of these can you do this month?

Charity ties it all together. Kindness, patience, forgiveness, giving. Charity is the belt that holds them all together. Put it on above everything else. ... And above all these things put on charity, which is the bond of perfectness. Colossians 3, verse 14. ... Think on this. What would your week look like if you put on charity first?
